thread:
Sara (CS): heads up — Acme reported a big change in answer quality after last night's deploy. they say more hallucinations and worse factuality on knowledge-base queries. ticket CS-4821 created.
Mike (Support): copying convo from customer: 'we hit dozens of responses where the assistant invents dates/people. this used to be tight.' they attached prompt+responses.
Sara (CS): repro steps from customer: 1) POST /v1/chat with model redwood-3b (they were using) 2) system prompt: 'You are an expert on Acme product docs.' 3) prompt: 'When was feature X launched and who signed off?' -> before deploy returned correct: 'Jan 12 2024, sign-off by Jane Doe' -> after deploy returns 'Feb 2025, signed off by an engineer named Mark' (wrong).
Aman (Eng): which model variant did they hit? logs show `model=redwood-3b-draft-sampling` in the canary group yesterday at 02:13 UTC. DeployBot: canary rollout 3b-draft-sampling -> 5% traffic at 2026-02-28T02:00Z.
Lena (ML): ah ok that matches. We had an experiment enabling speculative decoding + draft sampler on some traffic to reduce latency and token counts. Could increase entropy if mixing beam-like preds with sampling.
Elaine (PM): customer is paying prod traffic and flagged this as regression. CS wants a hotfix. Is rollback feasible?
Aman (Eng): we can pin Acme to stable redwood-3b-v1-stable immediately. quick rollback for whole canary is also possible — we planned a progressive ramp but can abort.
Sara (CS): customer asked for a mitigation ASAP — please confirm ETA.
Aman (Eng): ETA ~30m to pin their tenant to stable. I'll need @Lena to confirm that's the right fix (does it reduce latency too much?).
Lena (ML): pinning to v1-stable removes draft sampler; quality should return. Latency might increase ~15% for long contexts but within their SLO. Also we should check sampling temperature and top_k changes in the draft sampler config — those were loosened in the experiment.
Mike (Support): adding customer's sample payload and diffs below (pasted):
```
# request
POST /v1/chat
{
  "model": "redwood-3b-draft-sampling",
  "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"Expert on Acme docs"},{"role":"user","content":"When was feature X launched and who signed off?"}],
  "temperature": 0.0
}
# response (after deploy)
"Feature X was launched in February 2025 and signed off by Mark Spencer."
# response (before deploy)
"Feature X was launched on January 12, 2024 and was approved by Jane Doe (Product Lead)."
```
Sara (CS): customer insists they used temperature 0.0, so deterministic behavior expected.
Lena (ML): interesting — speculative decoding can interact badly with deterministic temps if draft/sample fallback path is mixing nonzero sampling heuristics; might be a bug where temperature override isn't enforced for the draft path. I'll repro locally.
Aman (Eng): logs show `sampling_mode=draft, temp_effective=0.7` on some requests — that is wrong. tracing user request id 3b-req-9912.
Elaine (PM): ok this is high priority. action items?
Lena (ML): immediate: 1) confirm pin to v1-stable for Acme (Sara/Aman) 2) reproduce locally with the exact payload + trace id (Lena/Aman) 3) check the draft sampler codepath for temperature propagation (Lena) 4) run quick metric diff on canary vs control for hallucination rate (Aman/Mike)
Aman (Eng): I'm on pin now. running tenant pin script.
Sara (CS): telling customer we'll pin them and keep them updated.
DeployBot: tenant-pin ACME -> redwood-3b-v1-stable applied (job id 8342).
Mike (Support): started a quick automated eval on 200 KB-style QA prompts, comparing canary vs stable. baseline shows ~3% hallucination; canary preliminary 9%. pushing full run.
Lena (ML): I reproduced locally using 3b-draft-sampling + temp 0.0 and saw inconsistent token logits: the draft scorer sometimes skipped temperature clamp before resampling. that's a bug.
Aman (Eng): opened internal bug RED-7756 to stop draft sampler from overriding request temperature. PR incoming.
Elaine (PM): target hotfix timeline?
Aman (Eng): hotfix PR + canary deploy today, ~3h to review + 1h to monitor. if urgent we can rollback whole experiment immediately.
Sara (CS): customer response: 'thank you, we appreciate the quick action. please keep us posted.' they asked for SLA credit if regression impacted product events.
Elaine (PM): note potential credit request — ops/finance will evaluate after rollback.
Mike (Support): full eval finished — canary hallucination 8.7% vs stable 2.9% on our 2k prompt set. attaching summary in the ticket.
Lena (ML): follow-up: we should add unit tests for temperature propagation in the draft sampler code and a synthetic eval for determinism-sensitive workloads.
Aman (Eng): rolling back the experiment to 0% now. DeployBot: canary rollback redwood-3b-draft-sampling -> 0% (job id 8351).
Sara (CS): customer updated: 'we see quality restored after your mitigation, thanks.' closing loop.
Elaine (PM): great fix. next steps: postmortem, add test, and update rollout checklist to include deterministic workload checks when enabling speculative/draft features.
Lena (ML): I'll write a short doc on known interactions between speculative decoding and temperature handling.
Aman (Eng): PR #1723 created for hotfix, linking RED-7756 and CS-4821.
Sara (CS): marking customer case resolved, leaving follow-up items in ticket. :white_check_mark:
Mike (Support): adding final note: keep an eye on other tenants in canary for similar upticks. we should run the hallucination diff sample across all canary tenants weekly until changes stabilize.
Elaine (PM): thanks everyone. closing this thread once PR merges and postmortem posted.
